newsitem.title: OMAN: OIB chairman resigns in line with new law.
newsitem.headline: OIB chairman resigns in line with new law.

text.p: Oman International Bank Chairman Omar bin Abdul Muniem al-Zawawi announced his resignation in line with new laws prohibiting ministers from holding directorships of public companies.

"I am pleased to announce to you my resignation as the chairman of the board of directors of Oman International Bank, in compliance with the provision of the Basic Statute of the State," he said in a statement with the bank's 1996 results.
Zawawi is an adviser to Sultan Qaboos bin Said.
Oman's basic law, introduced in November, prohibits ministers from serving as directors in publicly-held firms.
The law says the measure would help ensure they do "not exploit their positions for personal gain".
Zawawi, who had held the post since the bank was formed in 1984, said the board had elected deputy chairman Noor bin Mohammed bin Abdulrahman as the new chairman.
